narrative:
The model estimates a 74% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs is the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. With 6–10 years overall, you sit in a range where many people begin exploring new opportunities rather than staying long-term. Closely related, the time you have spent in your current organization (1–5 years) is the second most influential element and also pulls the prediction toward departure. Employees who stay longer in one place tend to remain, but your relatively short tenure here signals higher mobility to the model.

The third important factor works in the opposite direction: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities actually pulls the prediction slightly toward staying. However, it is not strong enough to outweigh the first two influences.

Taken together, your experience profile suggests you are at a career stage where changing employers becomes more likely. The organization should discuss your long-term plans with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer growth paths, or improved recognition could increase your commitment. You may also wish to reflect on what would make staying more attractive before considering external moves. (218 words)
